messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of 10 kPa (≈0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water is only slightly below 0 °C.  
Using the Clapeyron relation for the solid–liquid equilibrium of water, the slope of the melting curve near 0 °C is about 120 kPa K⁻¹, giving

\[
\frac{dT}{dP}\approx \frac{1}{120}\;\text{K kPa}^{-1}\approx 8.3\times10^{-3}\;\text{K kPa}^{-1}.
\]

Thus a pressure drop of 10 kPa lowers the freezing point by roughly

\[
\Delta T \approx 10\;\text{kPa}\times 8.3\times10^{-3}\;\text{K kPa}^{-1}\approx 0.083\;\text{K},
\]

so the freezing point is about **–0.08 °C** (essentially 0 °C within experimental uncertainty).
